title: Fire Safety
summary: Workers need training on fire hazards and on what to do in a fire emergency. Exits must be clear, and fire prevention means controlling ignition sources and flammable waste.
talking_points: Learn the fire hazards of your job and what to do in a fire emergency.
Know the evacuation routes and procedures before a fire starts. Everyone must be accounted for after evacuating.
Exit doors must never be blocked or locked while people are inside. Exit routes must be free of obstructions and marked with exit signs.
Know the alarm that signals a fire emergency, such as bells, whistles, horns, or voice communication.
Only use a fire extinguisher if you have been trained. Hands-on training is needed if workers are expected to use one.
Control ignition sources such as smoking, welding, and burning.
Store and clean up flammable materials and flammable waste properly.

Keep flammables away from heat-producing equipment such as burners, boilers, ovens, and stoves. Where a fixed fire suppression system is installed and out of service, a trained fire watch must respond to fire emergencies.
site_hazards_to_check: Blocked or locked exit doors and routes
Flammable waste and materials stored or piled up near ignition sources
Welding, burning, or smoking areas without controls
Heat-producing equipment with flammables stored nearby
Installed fire suppression system out of service with no fire watch
discussion_questions: What is our fire alarm signal, and where do we go when we hear it?
Which ignition sources on this site are closest to flammable materials?
Who here has been trained to use a fire extinguisher, and who should just evacuate?
